title: Hittite royal archive found in Turkey
summary: Archaeologists have discovered a significant Hittite royal archive in Turkey, containing thousands of cuneiform tablets that shed new light on the ancient Hittite Empire's administration, diplomacy, and daily life during the 13th century BCE.
problem_solved: Provides rare primary source documents that help historians understand Hittite governmental records, international treaties, and cultural practices that were previously poorly documented.
why_valuable: This discovery represents one of the most important archaeological finds in recent years, offering unprecedented insights into a Bronze Age civilization that bridged Anatolia and the ancient Near East.
